title: Take a bank card from a wallet, insert it chip-first into an ATM, press RETURN CARD, and put the card back
instruction: You are at a cash machine, holding your wallet in your left hand. Slide your bank card out of the wallet and insert it into the ATM's card slot, chip end first and chip facing up, until the reader takes it. Then press the key beside RETURN CARD on the screen (the lowest key on the right). When the reader pushes the card back out, take it and slide it back into the wallet.
context: Most adults use a cash machine: 54% of US adults used an ATM in the past year (YouGov Profiles, November 2024 to November 2025), and US ATMs still dispensed 3.4 billion cash withdrawals in 2024 (Federal Reserve Payments Study). At a chip ATM the customer takes the card from a wallet, pushes it into the reader slot chip end first, and the reader draws it in. The screen then lists services beside the keys either side of it; the customer presses the key beside the one wanted, here RETURN CARD, and the reader pushes the card part way back out to be taken and put away before the machine captures it. The physical difficulty: a 0.76 mm card slid out of a snug wallet pocket, turned and pushed into a closed slot about 3 mm high and about 2 mm wider than the card on each side, at an NCR ATM's reader height and depth; the right key of eight picked by its on-screen label and pressed in; the ejected 30 mm stub pinched against the fascia; and the card slid back into a 6 mm pocket.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); bench top z 0.7475. (1) An ATM front at true size, laid out as an NCR SelfServ 22e, fixed, in front of the right arm: a steel shelf 20 mm thick on the bench (top z 0.7675) whose front edge is 152 mm in front of the fascia face, and an orange fascia 476 mm wide and 700 mm high at x 0.426 in a blue cabinet with a privacy hood. Its card reader slot is centred at (0.42, -0.20, 1.0165), 249 mm above the shelf (NCR SS32 Site Preparation B006-6585-B000: card reader 1039 mm above the ATM base and 152 mm back from the shelf front; shelf top taken as 790 mm, an estimate), in an 80 x 60 mm green-lit bezel 6 mm proud of the fascia on a round orange boss. Above it, a 15 inch display (305 x 229 mm) in a 410 x 290 mm dark surround, centred 136 mm to the reader's left and 213 mm above it, with four round side keys (20 mm caps, 3 mm travel, sprung, about 3 N at full travel) each side, 178 mm from the screen centre, in rows 50 mm apart, the lowest 120 mm above the reader. The screen reads SELECT A SERVICE, and beside the keys, top to bottom, on the right: CASH, BALANCE, STATEMENT, RETURN CARD; on the left: FAST CASH, DEPOSIT, PIN CHANGE, OTHER. The RETURN CARD key is at about (0.41, -0.242, 1.137). Receipt slot, info plate, 4 x 4 keypad and the cash dispenser shutter as on the 22e. Behind the slot, a motorized reader at the Nidec Sankyo ICT3K5-3R6940's size (89 x 167 x 43 mm) with a closed throat 58 x 3 mm and a 15 degree lead-in (estimates). (2) A brown leather vertical card wallet, two leaves 72 x 85 mm open flat and upright, facing the robot, fixed (held in the left hand: the left gripper closes on the left leaf's top edge); the right leaf's pocket (6 mm between its panels, 58 mm wide) is centred at (0.25, -0.15), its floor 39 mm above the wallet's bottom edge at z 0.7525. (3) One ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 card, 85.60 x 53.98 x 0.76 mm, 5 g, gold chip near one short edge, stands in that pocket chip end down, chip facing the ATM, 40 mm out of it. The left arm holds the wallet; the right arm does the rest.
scoring: One tier per key substep, read from the card's pose, the reader's state, the side keys' joint travel and PhysX contact forces between the card and every robot link (fingers, pads, gripper housing, wrist, both arms). 0.25: the card out of the wallet (its lowest point 5 mm above the pocket mouth). 0.5: the reader has drawn the card in to its stop (it does so only for a card 20 mm in, chip end first and chip up, and let go). 0.75: with the card inside, the first key pressed (in 1.5 mm or more) is the one beside RETURN CARD; any other key first, or several at once, and the reader keeps the card (score stays 0.5). 1.0: the card, ejected and drawn out of the throat, back in the wallet's pocket (long axis within 15 degrees of vertical, lowest point within 4 mm of the pocket floor), let go no higher than 10 mm above the floor, no robot link touching it, still, for 2 s. Void, score 0: the card falls to the shelf, bench or floor. In a real trial a person checks the reader's log for the chip read (ICC answer-to-reset) and card-in, the video for chip end first and chip up and for the key pressed, and the wallet from a photo: the card stands 36 to 44 mm out of the pocket mouth (ruler) when seated, and from the side camera its top edge is no more than 10 mm above rest when the fingers open.
run_limit: 1,400 steps (70 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 in about 1,050 steps.
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Card in the wallet's pocket, chip end down and chip facing the ATM; reader empty and idle, keys out; both arms at their ready pose. About 1 minute.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the card is a free 5 g body gripped by friction alone. The side keys are sprung slide joints the robot pushes in. The reader's rollers are a scripted drive: once a card is 20 mm in the right way round and let go it sets the card's pose along the path (in, and out after RETURN CARD). The wallet is fixed in place (the left gripper only closes on it). Throat, trigger depth, stub, key force, timings and shelf height are estimates.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (1,049 steps, 52.45 s, GPU). Lazy routes (GPU): none 0.0; lift and put back 0.0 (dropped); pushed 12 mm 0.0 (falls out); chip face down 0.25; no key 0.5; wrong key 0.5; left in reader 0.75; drawn out then dropped 0.0; held 0.75; let go 40 mm up 0.0. Dream-1: 0.0.
failures: 1) Card pushed in tilted or chip down: it stops at the bezel or the reader does not take it: 0.25. 2) Wrong key pressed, or every key at once: the reader keeps the card: 0.5. 3) Key never pressed: the card stays inside: 0.5. 4) Card ejected but left in the slot: captured after 20 s: 0.75. 5) Card still held, or let go above the pocket floor: 0.75, or void if it falls out. 6) Card dropped on the shelf or bench: void, 0.
